dedupe_keys.name: venezuela june 2026 earthquake building debris assessment unep ocha joint environment unit

description: This data set estimates how much building debris the June 2026 earthquake in Venezuela produced and where it lies, to help plan debris removal. The producer is the Joint Environment Unit of the United Nations Environment Programme and OCHA, which published it on the Humanitarian Data Exchange. Coverage is the most affected Venezuelan states, from analyses between 24 and 27 June 2026. Damaged buildings were found by change detection on Sentinel-1 radar images, combined with Copernicus Emergency Management Service damage maps and checks on high-resolution optical imagery; debris volumes were then computed from building footprints with modelled heights from the Global Building Atlas. Results are given per damaged building and on 350 m and 3 km grids, with PDF maps in English and Spanish, including one for Caracas. The files are available as free GeoPackage and PDF downloads under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike licence. Caveats: the provider calls it a preliminary analysis not validated in the field, suitable for general planning only, and radar damage detection misses some damage and flags some false positives. Simulation uses: sizing debris collection, transport and disposal capacity after an earthquake, siting temporary debris storage, and a method template for other events. Related records: the Florida hurricane marine debris case (case_study-florida-hurricane-marine-debris-2016-2017) covers debris after storms.
name: Venezuela June 2026 earthquake: building debris assessment (UNEP/OCHA Joint Environment Unit)
provider: UNEP/OCHA Joint Environment Unit (Joint Environmental Emergency Team)
schema_summary: Debris quantities on 3 km and 350 m grids and per damaged building (GeoPackages), with PDF maps of quantities in English and Spanish and for Caracas; building footprints with modelled height from the Global Building Atlas, damage from Sentinel-1 change detection, Copernicus EMS EMSR884 and visual checks
